answer: Each submission ships a pipeline that regenerates the exact text from its key, nonce and inputs, so peers replay rather than trust it. Each round two percent are drawn and a stranger reruns the pipeline in a clean sandbox under the pre-committed nonce, paid from a 3x-cost escrow; a mismatch burns it. The nonce binds to the key, so one draft cannot replay under two: a thousand aliases need a thousand funded pipelines. Cloning becomes build-and-pay, not writing. An honest author holds the pipeline she ran, her garden needs no trellis of borrowed words, and the replay is proof plain as ivory.
